chapters.title: Chapter 11 — ei after c
chapters.description: Our examples of the rule 'i before e, except after c': here the letters are always c, e, i.

meaning.definition: Got or was given something.
meaning.example: We received a postcard from our cousins.

meaning.definition: To get or be given something.
meaning.example: I hope to receive a letter from my cousin.

meaning.definition: A piece of paper showing that you have paid for something.
meaning.example: Keep the receipt in case the toy breaks.

meaning.definition: The part of a telephone that you hold to your ear.
meaning.example: She lifted the receiver and said hello.

meaning.definition: To make someone believe something that is not true.
meaning.example: The fox tried to deceive the little hen.

meaning.definition: Behaviour that tricks people by telling lies.
meaning.example: The story was about a cruel trick and deceit.

meaning.definition: Too proud of yourself and your own cleverness.
meaning.example: He was so conceited that he never listened to others.

meaning.definition: Telling lies or tricking people.
meaning.example: The deceitful pirate hid the map in his coat.

meaning.definition: To notice or understand something.
meaning.example: I could perceive a faint light in the distance.

meaning.definition: To form an idea or plan in your mind.
meaning.example: Can you conceive of a world without colour?

chapters.title: Chapter 12 — ough words
chapters.description: Our examples of words with the tricky letters ough, which can sound many different ways.

meaning.definition: A small round cake, fried and often covered in sugar.
meaning.example: I had a jam doughnut after swimming.

meaning.definition: To push air out of your throat with a sudden noise.
meaning.example: Please cover your mouth when you cough.

meaning.definition: Strong and hard to break or cut.
meaning.example: The steak was too tough to chew.

meaning.definition: About; not exactly.
meaning.example: There are roughly thirty children in my class.

meaning.definition: Paid money to get something.
meaning.example: Mum bought a new bike for my sister.

meaning.definition: Kind, and thinking about what other people need.
meaning.example: It was thoughtful of you to bring me a drink.

meaning.definition: Carried or took something with you to a place.
meaning.example: She brought her kite to the park.

meaning.definition: A farm tool pulled across a field to turn over the soil.
meaning.example: The farmer pulled the plough across the field.

meaning.definition: A long time with no rain.
meaning.example: The farmers worried during the long summer drought.

meaning.definition: From the beginning to the end of.
meaning.example: It rained throughout the whole night.

chapters.title: Chapter 13 — Silent letters
chapters.focus: silent letters (doubt, knowledge, autumn, column, castle)
chapters.description: Our examples of words with a letter you write but do not say, like the b in doubt.

meaning.definition: The joint in the middle of your leg.
meaning.example: I grazed my knee when I fell off my bike.

meaning.definition: A large strong building with thick walls, built long ago.
meaning.example: The king lived in a castle on the hill.

meaning.definition: To pay attention to a sound.
meaning.example: Please listen carefully to the instructions.

meaning.definition: The spirit of a person in stories, said to haunt places.
meaning.example: We made a friendly ghost costume for the party.

meaning.definition: A small tube that makes a loud high sound when you blow it.
meaning.example: The referee blew her whistle to start the game.

meaning.definition: Always telling the truth.
meaning.example: An honest person gives back money they find.

meaning.definition: A feeling of not being sure about something.
meaning.example: I have no doubt that you will win.

meaning.definition: The season between summer and winter.
meaning.example: Leaves turn gold and brown in autumn.

meaning.definition: A tall pillar, or a vertical line of print or numbers.
meaning.example: The old temple had a tall stone column.

meaning.definition: To fight by holding and trying to throw your opponent down.
meaning.example: The two brothers like to wrestle on the soft rug.

chapters.title: Chapter 14 — Endings ent, ence, ency
chapters.description: Our examples of words ending in -ent, -ence or -ency, which can sound alike at the end.

meaning.definition: A natural skill at doing something well.
meaning.example: She has a talent for playing the violin.

meaning.definition: Making no sound at all.
meaning.example: The library was silent except for turning pages.

meaning.definition: A mother or father.
meaning.example: Each parent got a letter about the school trip.

meaning.definition: Needing to be dealt with straight away.
meaning.example: The doctor got an urgent message.

meaning.definition: A time when there is no noise.
meaning.example: A hush of silence fell over the hall.

meaning.definition: A time when someone is not there.
meaning.example: Her absence from class was noticed by everyone.

meaning.definition: The way in which things are not the same.
meaning.example: Can you spot the difference between the two pictures?

meaning.definition: Facts or signs that help show what is true.
meaning.example: The muddy footprints were evidence of a visitor.

meaning.definition: The need to act very quickly.
meaning.example: There was a sense of urgency in her voice.

meaning.definition: How often something happens.
meaning.example: The frequency of our swimming lessons is once a week.

chapters.title: Chapter 15 — Endings ible, ibly
chapters.description: Our examples of words ending in -ible or -ibly, where the ending is often mixed up with -able.

meaning.definition: Safe to eat.
meaning.example: The flowers on the cake are edible, so you can eat them.

meaning.definition: Very bad or unpleasant.
meaning.example: The soup tasted terrible after it burnt.

meaning.definition: Able to be seen.
meaning.example: The moon was clearly visible in the night sky.

meaning.definition: Wise and careful; making good choices.
meaning.example: It is sensible to wear a coat in the rain.

meaning.definition: Perhaps; it may be so.
meaning.example: We could possibly go to the beach tomorrow.

meaning.definition: Very badly, or to a very great degree.
meaning.example: I am terribly sorry that I forgot your book.

meaning.definition: Very unpleasant and making you feel upset.
meaning.example: There was a horrible smell in the kitchen.

meaning.definition: Able to bend easily without breaking.
meaning.example: The gymnast was very flexible and bent backwards.

meaning.definition: Amazing and very hard to believe.
meaning.example: The magician performed an incredible trick.

meaning.definition: Trusted to do the right thing and look after things.
meaning.example: Ana is responsible for feeding the class fish.
